title: evaluate_alert must skip when detector type differs from the type prepare routed on
answers: AI detector check ran on a worker without model credentials
What happens if the detector type is edited between prepare and evaluate?
How does CheckAlertWorkflow route to the LLM evaluate task queue?
body:
`CheckAlertWorkflow` picks the evaluate task queue in prepare from the detector type it read (`inputs.uses_llm_detector`); only the AI worker holds model credentials. `evaluate_alert` reloads the alert, so an edit in between can mismatch.
- Guard in `posthog/temporal/alerts/activities.py:evaluate_alert`: compares `is_llm_detector_config(alert.detector_config)` with `inputs.uses_llm_detector`; on mismatch logs `alerts.skip_detector_type_changed` and returns `EvaluateAlertResult(alert_check_id=None, should_notify=False, ...)` without touching `next_check_at`, so the next scheduler tick re-prepares and re-routes.
- Same skip style as the existing fingerprint guard.
- Tests must pass `uses_llm_detector` matching the alert's actual detector type (the executor-selection test was fixed to stop passing `not uses_llm_detector`).
applies: Alert evaluation Temporal workflow routing (LLM vs shared evaluate executor/queue)
